title: Federal Rule 24 — intervention
summary: Intervention is a procedure by which a person outside the lawsuit seeks to enter it to protect an interest or participate under the rule’s conditions. Rule 24 distinguishes intervention of right from permissive intervention.

sections.Role in the course: Intervention is a procedure by which a person outside the lawsuit seeks to enter it to protect an interest or participate under the rule’s conditions. Rule 24 distinguishes intervention of right from permissive intervention.
sections.What to examine: Identify the applicant’s interest, possible impairment, timeliness, and adequacy of existing representation, or the relevant basis for permissive intervention. Smuck illustrates why a government representative’s broad responsibilities may leave particular interests insufficiently represented.
